cards.explanation: The answer is that raiders had killed all the older sons. The raiders who came into the camp with the Arabs had killed all the older sons, so the people of Jerusalem made Ahaziah king (2 Chronicles 22:1). He was the youngest son of Jehoram. I think he never pictured wearing that crown.

The answer is mother. The text says she was his counselor in wickedness (2 Chronicles 22:3). Her name was Athaliah (2 Chronicles 22:2). Ahaziah walked in the ways of the house of Ahab with her voice in his ear.

The answer is destruction. The text says the house of Ahab counseled him "…to his destruction…" after his father died (2 Chronicles 22:4). Bad advice can sound friendly right up until the bill comes. Ahaziah followed it anyway.

The answer is Hazael king of Aram. Ahaziah went with Joram to fight against Hazael king of Aram at Ramoth-gilead (2 Chronicles 22:5). Aram was the nation on the other side of that battle. Ahaziah followed the counsel he'd been given, and it took him into that fight.

The answer is True. The text says "…the Arameans wounded Joram." (2 Chronicles 22:5). Joram was the king of Israel and the son of Ahab, and he came out of that fight hurt. Ahaziah had gone along, and the story keeps rolling from there.

The answer is that Ahaziah goes down to Jezreel to visit Joram. The text says he went because Joram had been wounded (2 Chronicles 22:6). Joram had returned to Jezreel to recover from the wounds the Arameans gave him. Sounds like a good friend, but hang on to that thought, friends.

The answer is God. The text says "Ahaziah’s downfall came from God when he went to visit Joram." (2 Chronicles 22:7). It wasn't bad luck or bad timing. The same verse says that when he arrived, he went out with Joram to meet Jehu son of Nimshi.

The answer is to destroy the house of Ahab. The LORD had anointed Jehu "…to destroy the house of Ahab." (2 Chronicles 22:7). And Ahaziah had been walking in the ways of that very house (2 Chronicles 22:3). When he arrived, he went out with Joram to meet Jehu.

The answer is rulers. Jehu found the rulers of Judah and the sons of Ahaziah's brothers, who were serving Ahaziah (2 Chronicles 22:8). The text says he killed them. This part is heavy, so I'll just say it plainly.

The answer is True. Jehu looked for Ahaziah, and Jehu's soldiers captured him while he was hiding in Samaria (2 Chronicles 22:9). Then Ahaziah was brought to Jehu and put to death. It's a heavy moment in the story.

The answer is that his grandfather Jehoshaphat sought the LORD. They said, "He is the grandson of Jehoshaphat, who sought the LORD with all his heart." (2 Chronicles 22:9). Jehoshaphat was Ahaziah's grandfather. His grandfather's heart toward the LORD is why the burial happened.

The answer is False. The text says "…no one was left from the house of Ahaziah with the strength to rule the kingdom." (2 Chronicles 22:9). The verse is about having the strength to rule. It's a sober ending, friends.
